description: RA-02 defense in depth for in-process role assumption. When a process runs with SYSTEM_ROLE (surface_runtime launches every surface with SYSTEM_ROLE=<surface id>; `pnpm surfaces` and `pnpm config-mission` set it for their own runtimes), withExecutionContext / withExecutionContextAsync may only assume the SYSTEM_ROLE itself, the shared core roles (narrow libs/core store-writer roles), or the roles listed for that system role here; anything else throws [ROLE_ASSUMPTION_DENIED]. A SYSTEM_ROLE without an entry may only assume itself. A may_assume or shared_core_roles entry can also name a store-grant issuance right that replaced a dedicated store role (G2, e.g. discussion_request_store, pr_publication_store): no role of that name exists, and the grant's facade applies the same rule before it issues the grant (libs/core/authority.ts assertStoreGrantIssuanceAllowed). Processes without SYSTEM_ROLE are unaffected. Lists are backed by the call-level reachability report computed in memory by scripts/analyze_role_assumptions.ts (not committed; `--write-report` writes it to active/shared/cache/system/role-assumption/; RN-02: call sites and role-forwarding wrappers walked from each entry point, including child processes that inherit SYSTEM_ROLE) and by opt-in runtime traces (KYBERION_ROLE_ASSUMPTION_TRACE, RN-01). The same bounds apply to a delegated child role (DR-01: a child spawned with buildExecutionEnv(env, role) under an inherited SYSTEM_ROLE runs as role only when this policy lets SYSTEM_ROLE assume it; the report counts each such call as an assumption site). A grant is only removed when the report proves it unreachable and no trace observed it; the role-assumption-reachability CI gate fails when a reachable role is missing. See knowledge/product/governance/AUTHORITY_MODEL.md section 3.B2.

shared_core_roles.rationale: Narrow roles that libs/core modules assume internally on behalf of their callers to write their own governed stores: pr_publication_store is not an authority role but the issuance right of the PR publication store grant (G2: libs/core/governance/pr-publication-runtime.ts checks it with assertStoreGrantIssuanceAllowed before each synchronous store access of a VCS host run, so every process that could assume the former shared role may still issue the grant and a SYSTEM_ROLE without an entry here still gets [ROLE_ASSUMPTION_DENIED]; assuming the name as a role is refused); infrastructure_sentinel (work coordination, peer messaging, mesh, the stimuli journal), audit_mirror_writer (write-only: the audit chain writes active/shared/runtime/audit-mirror/confidential/<tenant>/ through the seam libs/core/authority.ts registers, bound to the entry's tenant, whatever the caller's role; every process that records a tenant-scoped audit entry can reach it), knowledge_steward (mission creation), scope_locale_reader (read-only: libs/core/localization/locale.ts reads the tenant reply locale, knowledge/confidential/<tenant>/locale.json, bound to the turn's tenant, for every surface that renders a reply), peer_catalog_reader (read-only: libs/core/mesh/peer-conversation.ts reads the tenant peer transport catalog, knowledge/confidential/<tenant>/connections/peer-network.json, bound to the sending tenant, for every caller that sends a peer conversation message, and libs/core/mesh/peer-task-exchange.ts reads the tenant peer task catalog, knowledge/confidential/<tenant>/connections/peer-tasks.json, and checks the tenant profile knowledge/personal/tenants/<tenant>.json before an accepted task becomes a WorkItem, bound to the receiving tenant), peer_responder_reader (read-only: libs/core/mesh/peer-auto-reply.ts retrieves tenant knowledge for an opt-in peer auto reply, bound to the receiving tenant: that tenant profile, knowledge/confidential/<tenant>/ only, never its connections/ peer secrets), peer_task_artifact_writer (write-only to its own paths: libs/core/mesh/peer-task-exchange.ts stores an accepted peer task's report and log under active/shared/artifacts/confidential/<tenant>/report/peer-tasks/ and appends that tenant's artifact index, bound to the receiving tenant), metrics_cap_reader (read-only: libs/core/analysis/metrics.ts aggregateMetricsForEnforcement reads the partitioned metrics ledgers, bound to the caller's tenant, so the spend guard, budget governor and generation-cost dedup reached from any surface count every tier; it returns numbers only; its grant names no tenant), and the GovernedArtifactRole set of artifact-store / surface stores (chronos_gateway, slack_bridge, surface_runtime; surface-coordination-store maps a surface to its role from a governed plus a personal-tier map, so any GovernedArtifactRole is reachable wherever it is used). scope_locale_reader, peer_catalog_reader, peer_responder_reader and peer_task_artifact_writer are tenant-bound roles (libs/core/authority.ts TENANT_BOUND_READER_ROLES): their assumption throws [ROLE_TENANT_SCOPE_REQUIRED] without a valid tenant and [ROLE_TENANT_SCOPE_MISMATCH] when the caller has an active tenant that differs from the requested one, so a caller-supplied tenant never broadens access; a process without an active tenant (operator CLI, a server configured for one tenant) binds its own. operational_learning_writer is deliberately restricted to the system roles that reach its learning path. The broad roles (ecosystem_architect, mission_controller, sovereign_concierge) are never shared: each system role lists them only where the RN-02 analysis reaches them. The report shows oauth_callback_surface and surface_runtime do not reach some shared roles; they stay shared because removing a shared role for one system role needs a policy-shape change (tracked as a follow-up). chronos_tenant_runner and organization_operator are reached through the agent-runtime supervisor daemon child process (resident-dot sweep): chronos_tenant_runner lists and reads knowledge/confidential/<tenant>/dots/ charters bound to that tenant (same rule as chronos tenant pipelines), and organization_operator runs scheduled organization operation pipelines bound to the operation's tenant/organization (DL-06). Both are assumed internally by libs/core / the governed operation executor on behalf of whichever surface started the daemon, never by the surface itself. autonomy_learning_store is not an authority role but the issuance right of the tenant autonomy learning grant (G2: libs/core/governance/autonomy-action-state.ts checks it with assertStoreGrantIssuanceAllowed before it opens the opaque grant over the exact tenant autonomy outcome and override files, plus (MSN-STORE-BOUNDS-3) the outcome store's own write-time rewrite siblings (autonomy-outcomes.jsonl.compacting-*, .compact-out-*, .compact-restore-*) and files one level inside the partition's compaction-archive/; the caller keeps its role, bound to the store's tenant, and a caller bound to another tenant is refused; the store lock and retention audit stay outside the grant; assuming the name as a role is refused). credential_material_reader is not an authority role but the issuance right of the allocated credential material grant (G2: libs/core/secret/credential-allocations.ts checks it with assertStoreGrantIssuanceAllowed before it opens the opaque grant over the one admitted connection file knowledge/personal/connections/<service>.json; the caller keeps its role, bound to the allocation's tenant and the claim's mission/task; assuming the name as a role is refused). memory_provenance_reader is not an authority role but the issuance right of the memory provenance lineage read grant (G2: libs/core/knowledge/memory-provenance.ts checks it with assertStoreGrantIssuanceAllowed, and that a confidential read is for the caller's active tenant and a personal read for the owner NHI, before it opens the module-private synchronous grant over the one lineage state file; every I/O inside the grant is narrowed to that read; the caller keeps its role; assuming the name as a role is refused). person_charter_store is not an authority role but the issuance right of the person charter store grant (G2: libs/core/governance/person-charter-store-access.ts checks it with assertStoreGrantIssuanceAllowed inside the module-private synchronous grant of one exact person charter registry access or canonical personal reservation, which only an installed owner/NHI binding can open; the caller keeps its role and runs unbound; an installation whose policy does not name the right gets a grant that admits no I/O until the publication role migration registers it; assuming the name as a role is refused). personal_approval_store is not an authority role but the issuance right of the personal approval owner window (G2: libs/core/governance/personal-approval-runtime.ts checks it with assertStoreGrantIssuanceAllowed inside the module-private synchronous window over one exact owner file of the personal approval store (active/shared/runtime/tenant-approvals/personal/shared/owners/<owner-hash>/, or its Vitest copy), which only the approval store location opens and only for the caller's own personal owner; every I/O inside the window is narrowed to it, writes only under the personal owner partitions; the caller keeps its role and runs unbound; assuming the name as a role is refused). pipeline_journal_store is not an authority role but the issuance right of the tenant pipeline journal grant (G2: libs/core/pipeline/pipeline-run-journal.ts checks it with assertStoreGrantIssuanceAllowed before it opens the opaque grant over one confidential library pipeline run journal of the caller's own active tenant: the journal file, its writer lease and lease metrics; the caller keeps its role, bound to that tenant; the inter-process lock and every pipeline step stay outside the grant; assuming the name as a role is refused), so a tenant-bound charter role can record its run without gaining any tenant knowledge write. customer_decision_consumer_store (CD-09) is not an authority role but the issuance right of the consumer-lock grant (G2: libs/core/customer-decision/consumer-grant-access.ts checks it with assertStoreGrantIssuanceAllowed before it opens the opaque grant, for libs/core/mission/mission-decision-lock.ts at mission task boundaries (worker dispatch, record-task, record-evidence) and after a customer response, and for libs/core/customer-decision/store.ts asCustomerDecisionConsumerOwner on the operator facade's re-ask lock write; the grant names the case files read and the one consumer lock written, every write inside it is content-checked by the tier guard, the caller keeps its role, bound to the case's tenant; it never writes the ledger, an agenda or customers/; assuming the name as a role is refused). customer_decision_milestone_store (CD-10) is not an authority role but the issuance right of the bolt-review milestone grant (G2: libs/core/mission/mission-bolt-review.ts checks it with assertStoreGrantIssuanceAllowed when a mission starts, before it opens the opaque grant that names the agenda files read and the one agenda written, to mark the bolt-after:<mission> milestone passed on open bolt-review agendas; every write inside it is content-checked to append only milestones; the caller keeps its role, bound to the case's tenant; it never writes the ledger, a receipt, a consumer lock or customers/; assuming the name as a role is refused). tenant_ledger_store (D9) is tenant-bound and mediates only the bound tenant's partition of the hybrid ledger (libs/core/governance/ledger.ts: active/shared/runtime/tenant-ledger/<personal|confidential>/<tenant>/, read for the hash-chain tail and verification, appended for tenant records and tenant mission metadata) which libs/core/governance/ledger.ts assumes bound to the record's tenant; every process that records a tenant mission event or verifies ledgers can reach it. deliverable_inbox_writer (CD-10/CD-11 hardening) adds an operator task to the deliverable inbox only (libs/core/task/deliverable-inbox.ts addInboxEntry, from libs/core/mission/mission-bolt-review.ts and libs/core/customer-decision/operator-handoff.ts): the tier guard narrows its writes to active/shared/inbox/entries.jsonl and the inbox's own lock files, so the customer-triggered respond and the reminder sweep no longer borrow surface_runtime (which can write all of active/shared/runtime/). archived_mission_state_reader is not shared: it replaces mission_controller on the archived bolt state read of libs/core/mission/mission-decision-lock.ts and is listed per system role where the reachability report reaches it. tenant_approval_store is tenant-bound and mediates only the bound tenant's approval store partition (libs/core/governance/approval-store-location.ts: active/shared/runtime/tenant-approvals/<personal|confidential>/<tenant>/<channel>/ request records, passkey challenges and the channel event log), which the approval store assumes bound to the record's tenant for every tenant-scoped create, read, list and decision transition; every process that creates, lists or decides an approval can reach it. delegation_record_store is tenant-bound and mediates only the bound tenant's partition of the delegated-task store (libs/core/workforce/delegated-task-observability.ts: active/shared/runtime/delegation-records/confidential/<tenant>/ trace, records, child inboxes and the background-completion notification queue of libs/core/mission/delegation-notifications.ts), which the delegation store assumes bound to the delegation's tenant for every tenant partition read and write; every process that starts, settles, resumes or lists a delegation can reach it, and the store locks stay under the caller's role. tenant_approval_partition_index_reader is read-only and only lists the tenant directory names under active/shared/runtime/tenant-approvals/<personal|confidential>/ (descendant reads denied) so a process without an active tenant can find the partitions it then reads as tenant_approval_store; it is reachable wherever the approval store lists or locates a request. perception_media_worker is tenant-bound and mediates only the bound tenant's media-perception floors (scripts/lib/perception.ts withPerceptionMediaRole assumes it bound to the perception scope's own tenant: active/shared/tmp/<personal|confidential>/<tenant>/ and active/shared/staging/<personal|confidential>/<tenant>/, plus the semantic index subtree active/shared/cache/<personal|confidential>/<tenant>/perception/ only, read+write), giving the interactive see/listen/watch CLI — including its --index/--search semantic index stage — the same effective identity on its own scratch and index partitions that the claimed-WorkItem worker path already has; it never reads knowledge/, other tenants, the rest of the cache floor, system floors, or runtime state. actuator_playground_worker is tenant-bound and mediates only the bound tenant's actuator-playground scratch (scripts/actuator_playground.ts withPlaygroundScratchRole assumes it bound to the active scope's own tenant: active/shared/tmp/<personal|confidential>/<tenant>/actuator-playground/ only, read+write), giving interactive `pnpm playground` record/emit/sessions the same effective identity on its own tenant scratch — including child actuators that inherit MISSION_ROLE through buildSafeExecEnv — that the claimed-WorkItem worker path already has; it never reads knowledge/, other tenants, other domains on the tmp floor, staging, cache, or system floors. customer_decision_deal_note_writer is the tenant deal store (libs/core/organization/deal-store.ts asDealStore): tenant-bound, and only a tenant's deal files under knowledge/confidential/<tenant>/deals/ are read and written as it — reachable wherever a surface converses with a bound customer channel or an operator works a deal. customer_channel_binding_store is tenant-bound and mediates only one tenant's customer channel bindings (libs/core/organization/customer-channel-binding.ts reads knowledge/confidential/<tenant>/connections/channel-bindings.json bound to that tenant for inbound routing and the bind conflict check — reachable wherever a surface resolves an inbound customer channel; scripts/customer-channel/bindings.ts writes it), so no surface needs a confidential-tier grant to route a customer message. S4 slice 3 (ADR concept-model-v2 D6): the names of declared store grants (security-policy.json store_grants, listed in libs/core/foundation/declared-store-grant.ts: scope_locale_reader, peer_catalog_reader, peer_task_artifact_writer, first_job_tenant_status_reader, chronos_token_registry_reader, nhi_accountability_reader, reasoning_settings_writer, metrics_cap_reader, operational_learning_writer, customer_decision_deal_note_writer, credential_allocation_reader, tenant_ledger_store, delegation_record_store, tenant_approval_store, tenant_approval_partition_index_reader, audit_mirror_writer, ops_alert_store, workspace_tenant_registry_reader, workspace_tenant_registry_index_reader) are not authority roles but the grants' issuance rights: the store facade checks the same RA-02 rule with authority.ts withStoreGrant before it opens the grant, a tenant-bound grant keeps the [ROLE_TENANT_SCOPE_REQUIRED] / [ROLE_TENANT_SCOPE_MISMATCH] binding rule, assuming the name as a role is refused, and a process running as the name through env gets no I/O.

chronos_mirror_v2.rationale: Chronos compatibility app (MSN-KYBERION-SERVER-20261104): the operations console and its API moved into Concierge (/ops, /api/ops; see the concierge entry). This process only serves /api/healthz and answers every other request with a 308 to the Concierge origin (src/proxy.ts, resolveSurfaceBrowserUrl('concierge')); it assumes no role, so every former grant (chronos_localadmin / chronos_operator, dot_lifecycle_writer, generation_scheduler, reconcile_config_fallbacks, operational_learning_writer, …) was removed. The writers live in governed workers (dot_lifecycle_worker, generation_schedule).

computer_surface.rationale: ecosystem_architect: presence/displays/computer-surface/server.ts (/api/identity) and libs/core deployment-adapter / storage-janitor; sovereign_concierge: libs/core authn-providers module providers. ecosystem_architect, mission_controller, sovereign_concierge: reachable per the RN-02 analysis (scripts/analyze_role_assumptions.ts --write-report) (e.g. mission_controller via libs/core agent-identity appendGoverned and approval-gate, ecosystem_architect via libs/core deployment-adapter / storage-janitor, sovereign_concierge via libs/core authn-providers / browser-onboarding / tool-runtime-policy, and the GovernedArtifactRole union of surface-coordination-store). The surface also has unresolved sites (child processes that inherit SYSTEM_ROLE with a computed entry point, computed dynamic imports), so the analysis treats every role as reachable and nothing here is removable. chronos_token_registry_reader is deliberately absent: computer-surface/auth.ts passes `registrations: null` (TR-01), recorded as reviewed-infeasible in the report.

concierge.rationale: concierge_management_reader and concierge_management_writer are Concierge-only Web management mediators. Both require a server-bound exact resource capability checked before all ambient grants; the reader is mutation-free, and the writer additionally requires organization binding. They are intentionally not shared core roles. Concierge routes assume sovereign_concierge directly (config-missions, ingest, me, members, memory-queue, notification-preferences, plugins, progress, setup, training, work-inventory) plus libs/core authn-providers, browser-onboarding, slack-onboarding, tool-runtime-policy; withConciergeViewerContext assumes concierge_localadmin / concierge_operator; chronos_token_registry_reader: lib/viewer-context.ts and libs/core authn-providers read the chronos-access viewer token registry. ingest_commit (added by RN-03): /api/ingest runs scripts/ingest.ts as a child with buildExecutionEnv(process.env, ...), which keeps SYSTEM_ROLE=concierge, and the ceremony commits as ingest_commit (libs/actuators/ingest-actuator/src/commit.ts); Concierge can already assume ecosystem_architect, whose authority-role write scope (knowledge/, public and confidential tiers) covers the grant's allow_write paths, so this adds no effective authority. Since DR-01 the child runs as the delegated role sovereign_concierge (KYBERION_DELEGATED_ROLE, AUTHORITY_MODEL.md 3.B2) but keeps SYSTEM_ROLE=concierge, so its in-process ingest_commit assumption is still bounded by this entry and the grant stays. ecosystem_architect, mission_controller: reachable per the RN-02 analysis (scripts/analyze_role_assumptions.ts --write-report) (e.g. mission_controller via libs/core agent-identity appendGoverned and approval-gate, ecosystem_architect via libs/core deployment-adapter / storage-janitor, sovereign_concierge via libs/core authn-providers / browser-onboarding / tool-runtime-policy, and the GovernedArtifactRole union of surface-coordination-store). The surface also has unresolved sites (child processes that inherit SYSTEM_ROLE with a computed entry point, computed dynamic imports), so the analysis treats every role as reachable and nothing here is removable. workspace_graph_reader (MSN-SURFACE-UNIFY-20261103): the shared surface operation registry (libs/core/surface/surface-operation-registry.ts, HTTP /api/v1 and MCP kyberion.workspace.*) reads the workspace graph as this read-only role and filters rows by the caller's server-resolved viewer scope. Operations console (MSN-KYBERION-SERVER-20261104): Concierge serves the former Chronos console at /ops and its API at /api/ops; Chronos itself only answers 308 redirects and assumes no role. The /api/ops routes resolve the Concierge viewer and run viewer-scoped reads under chronos_localadmin / chronos_operator (lib/ops/ops-viewer.ts withViewerExecutionContext*, information-assets, plugin-host tenant registry reads), keeping the security-policy grants the console had; discussion_request_store is not an authority role but the issuance right of the opaque Discussion request receipt grant (G2; /api/ops/discussions POST, real selected tenant and an exact two-file request grant): libs/core/discussion/discussion-request-storage-scope.ts checks it with assertStoreGrantIssuanceAllowed (authority.ts) before issuing, so every other surface gets [ROLE_ASSUMPTION_DENIED]. engine_runtime_preferences_operator (Kyberion server phase 2, D3: moves with its route): 設定 › エンジン (/api/voice/engine-config, lib/engine-config-access.ts) saves the profile engine-runtime.json through libs/shared-voice/src/engine-runtime-preferences-operator.ts, which assumes the role only for a verified loopback localadmin principal inside its transaction; the route adds a loopback-peer, loopback-Host and Concierge mutation gate. D3: the high-privilege writers are deliberately absent. Workspace autonomy (/api/ops/workspace/autonomy) plans pause / resume / activate read-only (planWorkspaceAutonomyControl) and dispatches the write to scripts/dot_lifecycle_worker.ts under SYSTEM_ROLE=dot_lifecycle_worker (the only role that may assume dot_charter_store and dot_lifecycle_runtime_store); the schedule quick actions dispatch scripts/run_generation_schedule.ts under SYSTEM_ROLE=generation_schedule (generation_scheduler); both are audited as governed_worker_dispatch with the viewer principal. reconcile_config_fallbacks and operational_learning_writer are not reachable. H1: every other child the server spawns gets an explicit SYSTEM_ROLE=concierge (lib/server-child-env.ts, enforced by lib/server-child-env.test.ts), so a child is bounded by this entry and the absent writers fail closed instead of running unbounded.

customer_room.rationale: Customer-facing decision room (presence/displays/customer-room/server.ts, CD-07), operator-launched through surface_runtime with SYSTEM_ROLE=customer_room because it is exposed through the public ingress. The room assumes no role itself: it serves its page and runs the governed facade dist/scripts/customer_decision.js as a child for view / respond with a minimal explicit env (facadeChildEnv: the secure-io exec allowlist plus KYBERION_TENANT and KYBERION_ROOT) that does not carry SYSTEM_ROLE, so the facade assumes its own narrow tenant-bound roles (decision_ledger, customer_decision_invite_store, customer_decision_deal_note_writer) as when an operator runs it, and the RN-02 analysis reaches no role and no child process from this entry. Nothing to grant: an assumption from this process is refused.

dev_idp.rationale: scripts/dev_oidc_idp.ts run as surface 'dev-idp': a loopback-only throw-away OIDC provider. sovereign_concierge: oidc-login-settings.ts stores OIDC settings and the browser session key via secret-guard; audit_mirror_writer: secret-guard writes emit audit records. The IdP itself serves HTTP on 127.0.0.1 only.

discord_bridge.rationale: ecosystem_architect, mission_controller, sovereign_concierge: reachable per the RN-02 analysis (scripts/analyze_role_assumptions.ts --write-report) (e.g. mission_controller via libs/core agent-identity appendGoverned and approval-gate, ecosystem_architect via libs/core deployment-adapter / storage-janitor, sovereign_concierge via libs/core authn-providers / browser-onboarding / tool-runtime-policy, and the GovernedArtifactRole union of surface-coordination-store). The surface also has unresolved sites (child processes that inherit SYSTEM_ROLE with a computed entry point, computed dynamic imports), so the analysis treats every role as reachable and nothing here is removable.

dot_lifecycle_worker.rationale: Governed dot lifecycle worker (MSN-KYBERION-SERVER-20261104, D3): scripts/dot_lifecycle_worker.ts, launched by the Concierge /api/ops/workspace/autonomy route as a child with buildSystemRoleLaunchEnv(…, 'dot_lifecycle_worker') after the server checked viewer scope, workplace ownership, status and admission hash read-only. The worker only calls transitionDotCharterStatus (pause / resume / activate), which writes the charter under dot_lifecycle_writer; --expect-status, --expect-admission-hash and --expect-scope-json are mandatory and re-validated inside the charter lock, so a changed charter fails closed. Keeping the writer in this one-purpose process is why the Kyberion server itself never assumes dot_lifecycle_writer. | Flow decomposition (MSN-SCOPE-FLOWDECOMP-20261107): dot_lifecycle_writer was decomposed into dot_charter_store (charter documents, 3 custodies) + dot_lifecycle_runtime_store (lifecycle audit ledger, activation heartbeats, dot event-continuation state); inter-process locks run under the worker ambient role, which holds the active/shared/runtime/locks/ grant. The retired writer name is not assumable.

event_intake_surface.rationale: scripts/event_intake_surface.ts (loopback-only inbound event intake, operator-launched through surface_runtime with SYSTEM_ROLE=event_intake_surface). Assumes no role: ingestInboundEvent only appends normalized events to the dot events ledgers under active/shared/runtime/dot/, so no broad role (ecosystem_architect, mission_controller, sovereign_concierge) is granted.

generation_schedule.rationale: Recurring generation-schedule tick service (surfaces/generation-schedule.json, launched by surface_runtime with SYSTEM_ROLE=generation_schedule, entry dist/scripts/run_generation_schedule_daemon.js). Each tick runs under the generation_scheduler authority via GENERATION_SCHEDULER_AUTHORITY (scripts/run_generation_schedule.ts, libs/core/daemon/generation-scheduler.ts), so the daemon assumes only that role and no broad role (ecosystem_architect, mission_controller, sovereign_concierge). Child processes spawned mid-tick follow the scheduler scope through buildExecutionEnv (DR-01), so they stay on generation_scheduler.

imessage_bridge.rationale: ecosystem_architect, mission_controller, sovereign_concierge: reachable per the RN-02 analysis (scripts/analyze_role_assumptions.ts --write-report) (e.g. mission_controller via libs/core agent-identity appendGoverned and approval-gate, ecosystem_architect via libs/core deployment-adapter / storage-janitor, sovereign_concierge via libs/core authn-providers / browser-onboarding / tool-runtime-policy, and the GovernedArtifactRole union of surface-coordination-store). The surface also has unresolved sites (child processes that inherit SYSTEM_ROLE with a computed entry point, computed dynamic imports), so the analysis treats every role as reachable and nothing here is removable.

mcp_server_cowork.rationale: ecosystem_architect, mission_controller, sovereign_concierge: reachable per the RN-02 analysis (scripts/analyze_role_assumptions.ts --write-report) (e.g. mission_controller via libs/core agent-identity appendGoverned and approval-gate, ecosystem_architect via libs/core deployment-adapter / storage-janitor, sovereign_concierge via libs/core authn-providers / browser-onboarding / tool-runtime-policy, and the GovernedArtifactRole union of surface-coordination-store). The surface also has unresolved sites (child processes that inherit SYSTEM_ROLE with a computed entry point, computed dynamic imports), so the analysis treats every role as reachable and nothing here is removable. workspace_graph_reader (MSN-SURFACE-UNIFY-20261103): the shared surface operation registry (libs/core/surface/surface-operation-registry.ts, HTTP /api/v1 and MCP kyberion.workspace.*) reads the workspace graph as this read-only role and filters rows by the caller's server-resolved viewer scope.

nexus_daemon.rationale: presence/bridge/nexus-daemon.ts dispatches reflexes to the service actuator in-process, whose service reconciliation starts `node dist/libs/actuators/<id>/src/index.js` for any manifest id with process.env (SYSTEM_ROLE inherited), and dispatchFeedback runs the channel-registry connector actuator the same way: every actuator entry point is reachable. ingest_commit (ingest-actuator commit) and reconcile_config_fallbacks (system-actuator reconcile op) are therefore added by RN-03; nexus_daemon can already assume ecosystem_architect, whose authority-role write scope (knowledge/, public and confidential tiers) covers both grants' allow_write paths, so they add no effective authority. The actuator children are started with process.env and no explicit role, so they run as nexus_daemon (DR-01 delegation only applies to an explicit buildExecutionEnv role) and the grants stay. nhi_accountability_reader (NHI accountability read fix): nexus_daemon -> service/system actuator -> scripts/run_baseline_check.ts -> libs/core/agent/nhi-lifecycle-governance.ts listOrphanNhiIdentities resolves member status under this read-only role (knowledge/personal/members/ only, no writes); nexus_daemon can already assume ecosystem_architect, whose authority-role write scope covers knowledge/, so this adds no effective authority. ecosystem_architect, mission_controller, sovereign_concierge: reachable per the RN-02 analysis (scripts/analyze_role_assumptions.ts --write-report) (e.g. mission_controller via libs/core agent-identity appendGoverned and approval-gate, ecosystem_architect via libs/core deployment-adapter / storage-janitor, sovereign_concierge via libs/core authn-providers / browser-onboarding / tool-runtime-policy, and the GovernedArtifactRole union of surface-coordination-store). The surface also has unresolved sites (child processes that inherit SYSTEM_ROLE with a computed entry point, computed dynamic imports), so the analysis treats every role as reachable and nothing here is removable.

customer_decision_reader.rationale: Read-only customer-decision facade child of the Kyberion server: Concierge's /api/ops/customer-decisions overview, case and learning routes (presence/displays/concierge/src/lib/ops/customer-decision-overview-facade.ts) run dist/scripts/customer_decision_overview.js, which dispatches only the read-only `overview` verb (summary | --case <id> --detail | --learning), with --tenant bound by the server's viewer scope, under governedWorkerEnv('customer_decision_reader'). The facade reads the tenant decision ledger as decision_ledger; every other role the analysis reaches from this entry is a shared core role. The 15 unresolved (any role) sites in role-assumption-unresolved-baseline.json are the reasoning-provider CLI spawns (claude / codex / gemini / grok / cursor / devin / agy / opencode backends, provider discovery, the ACP mediator) reached only through module imports (scripts/customer-decision/common.ts → libs/core/customer-decision barrel → draft.ts → reasoning-bootstrap); the overview verb calls no reasoning backend, and any child such a site could spawn would inherit SYSTEM_ROLE=customer_decision_reader and stay bounded by this entry. Keeping the ledger role in this one-purpose child is why the Kyberion server itself never assumes decision_ledger; bounding the facade by SYSTEM_ROLE=concierge refused decision_ledger and broke every /ops customer-decision view. The writer verbs stay in scripts/customer_decision.ts, which this entry does not import.
